bug_semantics: CVE-2026-6745/GHSA-65fp-7g2v-658r claims CWE-79 XSS in Bagisto's Custom Scripts Handler up to 2.3.15. The public PoC (VulDB submit #794681, reporter hai271120) creates a custom admin role whose only ACL is Configure, logs in as that user, writes alert("XSS by haiiii") into Configure → General → Content → Custom Javascript, and shows the alert on the storefront (tab title Demo store, URL /). That path is the documented Custom Javascript feature: an administrator with configuration permission is meant to persist JS/CSS that the shop layout emits unescaped inside <script>/<style>. It is not neutralization of untrusted input.
flaw_origin: Not a vulnerability. Commit 4b6bb0a8f550e1a23391d4803de2910e1c526c7d (2020-09-03, jitendra@webkul.com) added general.content.custom_scripts.custom_css/custom_javascript and first wrote {!! core()->getConfigData(...) !!} into shop layouts with message 'Config to add custom css and javascript (Eg. google anlytics)'. Later Vue 2 layouts copied the same intentional sink (shop index, admin anonymous login, admin CSS). The advisory mislabels that first-party feature as XSS.

Vendor quote on the CVE is boilerplate also used on CVE-2026-6744: 'We already replied on the github advisories. All the security issues are addressed through security advisory. We will fix this in our upcomming releases.' That is not a confirmation of this Custom Scripts claim and is not a patch.

Public exploit folder https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/10p6SYcSVyfaaTg_dgItzMJvqixcmKnHR (CVE reference, tags=exploit): 'step by step exploit xss.docx' (Google Doc 19zr6w4_qcjB5GRhg7FIYJWa9yMx6c0BbdghBxmurxgo) steps: (1) default admin creates role with Configure only; (2) create user hai271120@yopmail.com; (3) login as that user; (4) Configure → General → Content, inject alert("XSS  by haiiii") into Custom Scripts, save; (5) alert popup 'all page'. Screenshots: Custom Javascript textarea at /admin/configuration/general/content with that payload and empty Custom CSS; role 'role config' with only Configure checked; alert dialog on storefront tab 'Demo store' at http://localhost:8082/ (not /admin).

Bagisto docs describe Custom Scripts as an admin feature to append CSS/JS (chat widgets, analytics): https://docs.bagisto.com/configure/content.html and https://docs.bagisto.com/configure/custom-scripts.html. Admin UI copy: 'Custom scripts are personalized pieces of code created to add specific functions or features'.

Parent cc2318066454d48c585ddab89a536e1b87d72f35: git grep custom_scripts|custom_javascript|custom_css on those three files exits 1 (absent).

v2.3.15 (advisory range) still emits the same config via {!! !!} in packages/Webkul/Shop/src/Resources/views/components/layouts/index.blade.php (CSS+JS), packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Resources/views/components/layouts/anonymous.blade.php (CSS+JS on login), and admin index.blade.php (CSS only). HEAD/v2.3.16/v2.3.19/v2.4.10 still contain custom_scripts.custom_javascript in shop and admin anonymous layouts; no sanitizer, no patched version. That persistence is expected for an intended feature, not a missing XSS fix.

ACL is a single 'configuration' key (packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Config/acl.php) covering admin.configuration.store. Granting Configure is granting the documented right to write storefront JS. The PoC attacker is that privileged admin using Custom Javascript as designed; this is a false positive / not a security issue, not CWE-79.
reasoning: Vulnerability-first: mine the CVE.org/NVD/GHSA records (still published, not withdrawn/rejected), then the only first-party exploit reference (Google Drive PoC). The PoC payload is literal JavaScript placed in the Custom Javascript setting by a user who was explicitly given the Configure ACL, and execution is demonstrated on the shop homepage. Source and docs show that setting is stored and printed with Blade {!! !!} into a <script> tag so merchants can add analytics. That is trusted, permission-gated script injection, not improper neutralization of untrusted HTML. Because the advisory itself is wrong, the verdict is FALSE_POSITIVE (not NOT_AI). No BIC or fix SHA is required: there is no vulnerable mechanism to introduce or patch. Feature-origin commit 4b6bb0a8 is human Webkul (jitendra) with empty trailers; AI was not judged because there is no vulnerability.
